long_biography.plain_text:
GEA was already a substantial family industrial company when Otto Happel took charge in his mid-twenties. Founded by his father and run for decades by his mother, it gave the newly qualified engineer an established platform rather than a blank-sheet start. Happel changed its trajectory through international expansion, process-engineering diversification and a sustained acquisition programme.

Happel took GEA public while retaining family voting control. In 1999, he sold the controlling stake to Metallgesellschaft for cash and shares, then increased his holding when the combined company faltered and helped drive its restructuring. Happel eventually sold the remaining position. He subsequently chaired Luserve, a Swiss wealth-management company, before leaving its board, completing his transition from industrial operator to investor.
